question: Q1: In adult humans, what are the bony attachments of the pectoralis major, which glenohumeral joint actions does each of its clavicular and sternocostal portions contribute to, and does the relative contribution vary with humeral position? Q2: In healthy adults performing supervised resistance training, does a programme using the barbell flat bench press differ from one using the bilateral standing cable fly at shoulder height in pectoralis major hypertrophy, and secondarily in task-specific maximal strength, when training variables are equated or reported?

synthesis:
SBLA-009 evidence packet for the vertical slice: pectoralis major, barbell flat bench press (Exercise X) and bilateral standing cable fly at shoulder height (Exercise Y).

HEADLINE. The primary comparative question has no answer in the retrieved literature. No study of the index cable fly as defined in research/questions/SBLA-008-vertical-slice.md section 3.2 was retrieved by any route, and no study comparing the barbell flat bench press with any cable fly for a pectoralis major size outcome was retrieved. That absence is reported as absence. It is not evidence of equivalence and not evidence of ineffectiveness. Under the frozen U2/EU2 decision Y was not widened and no related condition was pooled into the primary comparison.

FOUR-STATE RECONCILIATION. Records retrieved 1361. Duplicate retrieval events 252. Unique records after deduplication 1109. Excluded 1009. Awaiting full text 24. Included 76. Equation one, unique after deduplication = excluded + awaiting-full-text + included: 1109 = 1009 + 24 + 76, closes. Equation two, records retrieved = duplicates + unique after deduplication: 1361 = 252 + 1109, closes.

HOW THIS PACKET USES ITS TWO ARRAYS. includedSourceIds carries all 76 included sources. exclusions[] carries only the substantive exclusions of records that reached stage 3 as candidate evidence, plus the two retracted records and the four linked secondary reports. The remaining stage-1 exclusions are summarised by code here and enumerated one record at a time in research/screening/SBLA-009-screening-flow.json, which is authoritative for reconciliation under the frozen SE-U2/SU8 decision. Duplicates are deduplication events and appear in neither array; awaiting-full-text records are neither included nor excluded and appear in neither array; both are carried by count above and per record in the companion. No duplicate and no awaiting-full-text record is encoded here as a substantive exclusion.

EXCLUSION CODE COUNTS ACROSS ALL 1,009 EXCLUDED RECORDS: E-POP-5=236, E-POP-4=157, E-POP-1=150, E-EXP-3=110, E-OUT-2=90, E-EXP-1=73, E-OUT-1=40, E-REC-5=39, E-POP-6=18, E-DES-5=17, E-DES-4=15, E-OUT-5=15, E-REC-6=14, E-POP-2=7, E-EXP-7=6, E-DES-3=5, E-DES-6=5, E-EXP-2=4, E-REC-2=4, E-REC-4=2, E-EXP-4=2. Five codes were added by a dated, post-hoc, administrative amendment recorded in the screening-flow companion (AM-1): E-REC-5, E-REC-6, E-REC-7 (reserved, not issued), E-EXP-7 and E-DES-6. A post-hoc amendment cannot raise the certainty of any claim.

WHAT THE EVIDENCE DOES SUPPORT. Twenty-two draft claims and five absence records are in content-drafts/syntheses/SBLA-009-atomic-claims.json. The best-supported finding is that the pectoralis major is regionally differentiated: measured moment arms, segmental and high-density electromyography, shear-wave elastography, cadaveric innervation and exercise activation all converge on it, at moderate certainty. The muscle is among the principal glenohumeral adductors by measured moment arm, at high certainty. Chest resistance training increases pectoralis major thickness, at low certainty, from two small usable trials. At matched percentages of body weight a standing cable cross-over of unreported pulley height produced significantly larger shoulder joint moments and a far smaller elbow excursion than a flat barbell bench press, at low certainty, from one study of twenty participants. No claim in this packet uses the word better, and no claim makes a press-versus-fly hypertrophy statement.

SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS. The pre-specified within-participant contralateral-limb sensitivity analysis required by the frozen U3/EU1 decision contains zero eligible studies. The specification was fixed before results were seen and is retained. Every included tier-1 study uses a between-participant contrast.

SECONDARY QUESTION. Regional clavicular-versus-sternocostal hypertrophy, kept secondary by the frozen U4/EU3 decision, has one small site-specific tier-1 result in the direction the activation evidence predicts, and nothing else. It does not replace or upgrade the whole-muscle outcome.

CONTRADICTIONS FOUND AND KEPT. Nine are mapped in research/syntheses/SBLA-009-synthesis.md section 3, including two disagreeing press-versus-fly activation studies, a cadaveric series contradicting the standard bilaminar description of the humeral enthesis, primary innervation series contradicting the two-nerve textbook account, and a published statement by the group that measured bench press activation most carefully that the inclination literature is contradictory because of measurement artefact. Two retracted papers (PMID 31188644 and PMID 30779716) were retrieved by the contradiction stratum and are blocked from supporting any live claim.
